div.p: In order to support the different maturity levels foreseen for the European EHR eXchange format (structured, text-only, unstructured), this version of the guide does not impose the mandatory presence of entries in the Discharge Report sections.
However, the presence of entries in the Discharge Report sections is generally recommended to ensure a more structured and interoperable document.
This recommendation is expressed in this guide through specific obligations which guide implementers toward achieving a higher level of data quality and interoperability.

This profile applies to any kind of discharge report. The kind of report is conveyed by Composition.type, bound (extensible) to the Discharge Report Type value set: for example LOINC 34105-7 (Hospital Discharge summary) for a hospital discharge report, or LOINC 59258-4 (Emergency department Discharge summary) for an emergency department discharge report. The generic code LOINC 18842-5 (Discharge summary) is used when no more specific code applies. The kind of encounter is described by Encounter.class and Encounter.type of the encounter referenced by Composition.encounter.

Sections that are not relevant for a given kind of encounter are simply omitted; national or setting-specific guides may further constrain this profile, for example by requiring sections or fixing the document type.
To address the Discharge Report Structure Challenge , we have opted for a flexible approach rather than imposing a rigid format.

The "flat structure" documented in the guide should be understood as a sort of "section library" that can be reused in both flat and nested structures. This approach allows implementers to organise the report according to local or institutional needs while maintaining a standardised content model.
The flat structure is nevertheless considered best practice. Where sub-sections are needed, see this example of how they can be used.

ol.li: At least one of the Discharge summary or Course of encounter sections SHALL be present (invariant cmp-dr-2).
Section slices are open, meaning that implementers have the freedom to include additional "first-level" sections.
With the exception of a few specific cases, sub-sections are allowed, giving healthcare providers the ability to create a structure that best fits their clinical context.

div.p: By offering this level of flexibility, the implementation guide supports diverse healthcare environments while promoting consistency in content and interoperability.
div.h3: Determining whether a condition was present on admission
div.p: The timing of the condition may be used to determine whether it was already present at the time of admission or developed during the encounter (e.g. the hospital stay). In particular, Condition.onset[x] may be compared with the admission date and time, or with the start of the referenced encounter.
Condition.category may also provide contextual information about the role of the condition; however, no specific category is defined by this guide for this purpose.
div.h3: Determining the timing of observations relative to the admission
div.p: Similarly, the relevant elements of an observation can be used to determine whether it occurred before, during, or after the admission, and to establish the chronological order of observations within the encounter. This may be determined from Observation.effective[x],compared with the period of the encounter referenced by Composition.encounter and/or from the encounter referenced by the observation.
